items.quantitative_outcome: none stated. The reported move is a multi-year license to de-identified multimodal oncology data through 2031, plus access to Tempus’s Lens platform for BMS researchers.
items.signal: Potentially distinctive data access for oncology discovery and development; the available report describes the data and platform access but gives no measured operating benefit.

items.quantitative_outcome: The report says an independent AI-assisted central read produced confirmed objective response rate and confirmed disease control rate “consistent with local investigator-assessed outcomes.” No numeric result or improvement is stated.
items.signal: Prospective use of AI-assisted RECIST 1.1 assessment as an efficacy endpoint in a pharma-sponsored oncology trial; an early capability signal, not evidence of a quantified advantage over standard assessment.
items.source: Vysioneer announcement distributed by PR Newswire

items.quantitative_outcome: none stated. The release describes a planned Abu Dhabi programme with M42 to identify patients with uncontrolled hypertension and support clinical-trial recruitment; it reports no measured outcome.
items.signal: Potential access to governed, de-identified real-world data and clinical workflows through an international collaboration with Oracle and M42. This is an announced exploration, not a demonstrated benefit.

FactSet is integrating Nasdaq Private Market capitalization-table data, backed by auditable documentation and filings, into its platform. The source says this data could support due diligence, valuation and deal sourcing; it reports no measured operating benefit.
items.source: FactSet and Nasdaq Private Market press release (reported by GlobeNewswire)

items.signal: Monetary announced an AI-native municipal capital-markets platform combining public market data, proprietary firm intelligence, permissioned client data, and live market feeds. The release describes automated comparable analyses, pricing, debt sizing and refunding analysis, but gives no measured outcome.

Deutsche Bank deployed Farsight on-premises across investment banking and capital markets teams in Europe and North America. The announcement says the system can incorporate the bank’s prior work, internal standards and proprietary data into workflows; it reports no measured operating benefit.

Balyasny announced deployment of Gemini models in proprietary research platforms connected to more than 80 internal financial databases and enterprise tools. The announcement describes high-volume document ingestion and research synthesis but provides no measured time, accuracy, cost, or discovery-yield result.
items.source: Google Cloud and Balyasny Asset Management announcement

items.comparator: Year-over-year internal comparison; the release does not identify a separate control group. It also reports a customer comparison for MDR with endpoint coverage versus endpoint detection and response alone.
items.quantitative_outcome: The company’s report says: “agentic AI now resolves 60% of security investigations.” It also reports that monthly investigation volume increased 21% while alert volume declined 19%, and “the average time from an alert-generating event to an actionable ticket fell 36%.” For customers using Aurora MDR with endpoint coverage, it reports “seven times fewer events escalate to investigation” than for customers using endpoint detection and response alone.
items.signal: A large operational footprint and reported reductions in alert burden and time-to-ticket could indicate an advantage built on its security-event data and SOC operations. The evidence is company-reported, and no independent evaluation is cited in the release.
items.source: Arctic Wolf, 2026 Agentic Security Operations Report press release

items.comparator: The company reports comparisons against Argon, its previous flagship model, and an unnamed “another lab’s large frontier model”; specific benchmark baselines are not supplied in the result.
items.quantitative_outcome: Google’s reported results include “more than 10X better” performance than “another lab’s large frontier model” at generating high-quality patches, as reported by the Chrome team; internal teams reported a “nearly 80% drop in misalignment alerts.” Google also said Carbon “cuts unsupported claims by approximately 2x over Argon.”
items.signal: Reported patch-generation and reliability improvements in cybersecurity-relevant coding workflows are a potential capability signal. These are vendor-reported tests and internal reports, not independent operational evaluations.
items.source: SiliconANGLE, “Google debuts flagship Gemini 4 Carbon model with cybersecurity upgrades” (summarizing Google statements)

items.signal: The company announced early access to a cybersecurity-optimized variant of Mistral Large 4 through a design-partner program, with initial work focused on penetration testing, technical audits, incident investigation and response. Early model access combined with Orange Cyberdefense’s domain expertise is a distinctive partnership/data-access move, though the announcement provides no measured outcome.
items.source: Orange press release, “Orange Cyberdefense becomes Mistral AI's first European MSSP design Partner”

items.signal: A partnership gives Aquila Deep Intel access to Constella’s “extensive intelligence datasets, investigative platforms, and APIs” for cyber-intelligence services, initially focused on French-speaking markets. This is a distinctive data-access move that could support AI-enabled capabilities, but the announcement states no measured outcome.
items.source: EIN Presswire release, “Constella Intelligence and Aquila Deep Intel Announce Strategic Partnership to Advance Cyber Threat Intelligence”

items.comparator: Baseline/comparator not stated in the available report; the reported changes are from AI-managed beamforming trials in New York City, especially during peak hours.
items.quantitative_outcome: The report says the trials achieved “a 16% improvement in downlink user throughput, a 12% improvement in spectral efficiency and a 10% increase in downlink data volume.”
items.signal: AI-managed beamforming trial reported with quantified network-performance gains. This is a candidate weak signal; the reported trial results and unspecified comparison baseline do not establish a durable or hard-to-copy advantage.
items.source: TelecomTV, reporting T-Mobile US’s trial results

items.comparator: No measured comparison or baseline is stated in the available coverage; the figures are described as potential reductions for inspection preparation and production planning, not as independently verified outcomes.
items.quantitative_outcome: The article says Siemens reports “up to 85% less inspection-preparation engineering effort” and “up to 40% shorter time to market”; it also describes an “up to 20% production-planning cost” claim. These are presented as claims, not verified measured results.
items.signal: Industrial AI workflows for inspection preparation and production planning are a weak candidate: quantified potential benefits are reported, but the figures lack a stated matched baseline and independent validation.
items.source: LLM Scorebook, reporting on Siemens’s Erlangen factory announcement
